guides.title: How to get a driving licence in Europe
guides.description: Understand residence rules, national training requirements and the questions to ask before starting your first car driving licence in Europe.

sections.title: Start with the country where you live
paragraphs: There is no single application process for every European country. In the EU, applicants generally need to meet residence, age and medical requirements and pass theory and practical tests. Driving-school training is not governed by one EU-wide set of rules, so use the country guides below for the next step.

EU guidance normally places your application in the country of your usual residence: generally where you live for at least 185 days in a calendar year because of personal or work ties. Specific arrangements apply where those ties are in different countries. Studying abroad does not automatically transfer your usual residence, but you can apply in the host EU country after proving at least six months of study there.

sources.label: European Union: getting a driving licence

sections.title: Do not transfer one country's requirements to another
paragraphs: A shared licence category does not mean identical training. Sweden requires a learner's permit and valid risk education for a category B licence. Norway's published training route includes staged assessments and mandatory safety courses. These are different national systems, not interchangeable checklists.

This series starts with Germany, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Norway, France, the Netherlands and Spain. It does not yet cover every European country. The EU residence overview should not be treated as a complete statement of Norwegian or other non-EU national law.

sections.title: Compare the full cost, not just a lesson price
paragraphs: There is no guaranteed Europe-wide licence price. As an example, ADAC separates Germany's school charges, practical lessons, examination-body fees and supporting requirements. Its example budgets are not a quote for another country or an upper limit for an individual learner.

Use the school-comparison questions below to request a written breakdown. Do not assume an intensive-course timetable guarantees an examination appointment. This series does not promise school availability or booking through DriveLinkUp in every country.

guides.title: How to get a driving licence in Germany
guides.description: A first-time category B guide to German applications, first aid, theory tuition, special training drives, tests and school costs.

sections.title: Choose the first-time applicant route
paragraphs: To obtain your first German category B car licence, enrol at a Fahrschule, apply through the responsible licensing authority, complete training and pass the theory and practical examinations. First-aid training and an eyesight test form part of the application requirements.

Germany also offers accompanied driving at 17 through BF17. This is a separate route with accompanying-person requirements, not unrestricted independent driving at 17. Check the requirements with your local authority.

sources.label: German government: driving licence and mobility

sections.title: Prepare your application
paragraphs: The licensing office is commonly called the Fahrerlaubnisbehörde or Führerscheinstelle. Use its current checklist. Berlin, for example, lists identity documents, a biometric photograph, school and examination-centre details, first-aid proof and an eyesight-test certificate no more than two years old for category B. Berlin's checklist is a local example, not a guarantee of identical administration throughout Germany.

sections.title: Understand mandatory theory and practical training
paragraphs: For a first category B licence, ADAC lists 12 general theory sessions and two category-specific sessions, each lasting 90 minutes. The prescribed special drives are five rural-road, four Autobahn and three twilight or darkness units, each lasting 45 minutes.

Those 12 special drives are not the whole practical course. Ordinary driving practice is additional, and there is no fixed statutory minimum number of ordinary category B practice lessons. Your progress determines how much training you need.

sources.label: ADAC: theory lessons and special training drives

sections.title: Check test languages and budget carefully
paragraphs: English is available for the German theory test. Do not assume the same language arrangement applies to the practical test: ADAC states that the practical examination is conducted in German. Ask your instructor to prepare you for the instructions used during the test.

There is no fixed total price. Request separate amounts for school enrolment, materials, ordinary lessons, special drives, school test-presentation charges and examination-body fees. Extra lessons and repeat tests can raise the final bill; published examples are not guaranteed maximum costs.

guides.title: How to get a driving licence in Sweden
guides.description: Learn the Swedish category B process: learner's permit, private practice, risk education, theory and practical driving tests.

sections.title: Check category B eligibility
paragraphs: For a Swedish category B licence, Transportstyrelsen requires a valid learner's permit, permanent residence in Sweden or at least six months of study there, age 18, valid car risk education and passed theory and practical tests. Its checklist also says you must not already hold a licence from another EEA country; check exchange rules if you do.
You can begin practising in a passenger car without a trailer from age 16 if you meet the practice requirements. That is a learning age, not permission to drive independently.

sections.title: Apply for your learner's permit
paragraphs: Apply for a körkortstillstånd before starting driving practice. For category B, the application includes a health declaration and eyesight-test certificate. Transportstyrelsen assesses medical and personal suitability. The permit is valid for five years and cannot be extended.

If you practise privately, you need an approved accompanying driver, called a handledare. Transportstyrelsen's published guidance also requires the learner and accompanying driver to have completed the introduction course for private category B practice. Check current requirements before arranging private sessions.

sections.title: Complete risk education and the tests
paragraphs: The compulsory risk course has two parts. Part 1 covers alcohol, drugs, fatigue and other risky behaviour; part 2 addresses speed, safety and driving in particular conditions. Both parts must be completed and valid when you take the theory and practical tests.

The tests are taken through Trafikverket, the Swedish Transport Administration. Keep the permit, risk-course and test arrangements distinct when comparing school packages: buying lessons does not itself complete these requirements.

sources.label: Transportstyrelsen: learning to drive and risk education

guides.title: How to get a driving licence in Denmark
guides.description: Understand Denmark's category B application, medical certificate, first aid, mandatory school training and special rules at age 17.

sections.title: Check residence and age requirements
paragraphs: Denmark can issue a category B car licence from age 17, with special restrictions until age 18. Færdselsstyrelsen lists usual residence in Denmark, a medical certificate, traffic-related first aid, completed driver training and a passed driving examination among the requirements.
Practical training, including the manoeuvring area, cannot begin earlier than three months before your 17th birthday. The practical test cannot be taken before age 17.

sections.title: Apply through Borgerservice and complete training
paragraphs: Submit the licence application through municipal Borgerservice. The authority's car-licence guide lists a photograph, medical certificate and first-aid certificate among the supporting items. The municipality assesses whether you meet the conditions.

Driver training with an instructor is compulsory and combines classroom theory and practical instruction. Færdselsstyrelsen conducts the theory and practical examinations; your instructor helps arrange them after the necessary training. Ask the school to explain the current curriculum and everything excluded from its advertised package.

sections.title: Understand the restrictions at 17
paragraphs: Under the authority's published rules, a licensed 17-year-old may drive alone between 05:00 and 20:00, but must have an accompanying person between 20:00 and 05:00. Until turning 18, driving is restricted to Denmark. Parental or guardian consent is part of the under-18 application.

Do not confuse passing at 17 with unrestricted international driving. The temporary paper licence issued after a successful test is also valid only in Denmark. Check the accompanying-person requirements before your first evening drive.

guides.title: How to get a driving licence in Finland
guides.description: A Finnish category B guide to the driving licence permit, first-licence training, driving instruction, risk training and tests.

sections.title: Apply for the correct driving licence permit
paragraphs: You need a driving licence permit to take Finland's theory and driving tests. Apply for the first-licence permit only if you have not previously held a licence in Finland or abroad. If you already hold a moped or tractor licence, Traficom directs you to the licence-upgrade route instead.

The permit requirements include residence or qualifying study in Finland, fitness to drive, the relevant age and absence of a driving ban. A category B permit can be granted from age 16, but the ordinary car-licence age is 18. A permit at 16 is not an independent driving entitlement.

sections.title: Complete the required training
paragraphs: Traficom separates first-licence training, ordinary driving lessons and risk-recognition training. First-licence training is called EAS. It is not required again if you already hold a qualifying earlier licence such as a moped or tractor licence.

Ordinary driving instruction can be provided by a driving school or a person holding a driving instruction permit. EAS and risk-recognition training require an approved provider and cannot simply be delivered under the private driving instruction permit. Confirm the current training requirements and package contents with your provider.

sections.title: Pass the examinations and check your interim entitlement
paragraphs: For the ordinary age-18 route, the theory test can be taken one month before turning 18. The driving test follows a passed theory test and can normally be taken from age 18. A separate age-exception permit can allow testing at 17; do not assume it applies automatically.

After passing, the examination certificate and photo ID provide a temporary entitlement to drive in mainland Finland for up to six months while awaiting the licence. This is not a promise that the temporary documents are accepted abroad.

sources.label: Traficom: examinations and receiving your licence

guides.title: How to get a driving licence in Norway
guides.description: Understand Norwegian category B training stages, private practice, mandatory safety courses, theory testing and the practical test.

sections.title: Start with the basic traffic course
paragraphs: Norway's category B route is organised in stages by Statens vegvesen. The Basic Traffic Course normally provides the learner's permit needed for practice. People aged 25 or over are exempt from parts of this course, but still need the night-driving and first-aid modules. Check how the exemptions apply to your training record.

For passenger-car practice, you must be at least 16. A private accompanying driver must be at least 25 and have held the relevant licence continuously for the previous five years. The car needs the prescribed L sign and an extra mirror for the accompanying person.

sections.title: Progress through training and safety courses
paragraphs: The stages cover basic vehicle skills, proficiency in traffic and final training, with mandatory assessments during progression. Training can combine a driving school and eligible private practice; the number of ordinary lessons depends on your needs and experience.

The published route includes a four-hour safety course on a practice range and a 13-hour safety course on the road. Mandatory courses alone do not guarantee test readiness. Your school should explain which training remains and how your progress is registered.

sources.label: Statens vegvesen: training stages and mandatory courses

sections.title: Apply and arrange the tests
paragraphs: Apply for the licence before booking the theory test. After passing theory, you can take the practical test when the other requirements are met and all mandatory training is registered. Track your application and training on the authority's Your Page service.

The practical-test car must be an approved test vehicle rented from a driving school. Ask the school to itemise test-car rental separately from lessons and examination fees so that you can compare the full budget.

guides.title: How to get a driving licence in France
guides.description: Learn the French permis B process, school and independent-candidate routes, registration, theory test and practical examination.

sections.title: Choose your permis B learning route
paragraphs: France allows applicants to obtain the category B car licence from age 17. The learning route matters: traditional driving-school training, early accompanied learning and the independent-candidate route have different requirements. Do not treat one route's training minimum as a rule for every applicant.

If you are under 21 and this is your first licence category, the official guide requires ASSR2 or ASR road-safety certification. Other eligibility and document requirements depend on your circumstances; use the official checklist before registration.

sections.title: Register and prepare the theory examination
paragraphs: Your driving school can handle examination registration, or you can register yourself. The official process uses ANTS; where the school creates an account on your behalf, you must activate it yourself. The general theory test is called the code or ETG.

Theory can be prepared through a school or as an independent candidate. For the independent route, Service Public lists a €30 theory-test registration charge. That is not the full cost of obtaining a licence and does not include practical training or vehicle arrangements.

sections.title: Respect the rules for independent practice
paragraphs: Candidat libre does not mean unregulated driving practice. The official guide requires an eligible accompanying driver, learning documents and a compliant dual-control vehicle. It states that no minimum training-hour volume is imposed on that route. This should not be confused with driving-school training minimums.

Independent candidates book the practical examination through RdvPermis using their NEPH registration number and must provide the compliant examination vehicle. The practical examination lasts 32 minutes. Ask about vehicle rental, insurance and accompanying-driver requirements before choosing this route to save money.

sources.label: Service Public: candidat libre requirements and examination

guides.title: How to get a driving licence in the Netherlands
guides.description: Understand Dutch category B health declarations, CBR tests, supervised driving at 17 and collecting your first licence.

sections.title: Start with the health declaration
paragraphs: The CBR assesses fitness to drive through the Gezondheidsverklaring, a health declaration. Its car-licence guidance says to complete this at the beginning of your driver training through Mijn CBR. This is separate from demonstrating driving skill in the examination.

Answer the questions accurately and follow any further assessment instructions from CBR. Its examination terms require your physical and mental fitness to have been established before the practical test takes place. Do not assume booking lessons means this assessment has been completed.

sources.label: CBR: health declaration for a car licence

sections.title: Prepare for CBR examinations
paragraphs: CBR sets the procedures for theory and practical examinations. Bring accepted identification and follow the appointment requirements. Its published terms state that a passed theory result is valid for one and a half years. Plan your learning and practical examination around that validity rather than treating theory as permanent.

Request a written school quote separating lessons, theory preparation, CBR fees, health-declaration costs and any examination-vehicle or administration charges. Confirm test-language arrangements directly instead of assuming the instructor's teaching language will also be available in every examination format.

sections.title: Passing at 17 and collecting the licence
paragraphs: The Dutch government states that the minimum age for the practical car examination is 17. Those who pass at 17 must drive with a registered coach until age 18 and need a begeleiderspas, an accompanied-driving permit. Check those arrangements before applying for the licence.

After passing the practical test, apply through your municipality and collect the licence. The government explicitly says you must not drive until you have collected it. A successful test result alone is not permission to drive away.

sources.label: Government of the Netherlands: applying for and collecting a licence

guides.title: How to get a driving licence in Spain
guides.description: A first-time Spanish car-licence guide to DGT eligibility, the medical fitness report, school applications, examinations and provisional documents.

sections.title: Check eligibility with DGT
paragraphs: Spain's Dirección General de Tráfico, or DGT, lists residence, the required age, psychophysical fitness and passing the applicable theory and practical tests among the general requirements for a new licence. Applicants must not be disqualified from driving or already hold an EU or EEA licence in circumstances that require a different route.

If you already have a foreign licence, check recognition or exchange eligibility first. A first-time learner application is not automatically the correct or cheapest route for someone moving to Spain.

sections.title: Get the fitness report and submit the application
paragraphs: Obtain an informe de aptitud psicofísica at an authorised Centro de Reconocimiento de Conductores. Tell the centre which licence you are applying for. DGT says the report is valid for 90 days for submitting the examination application, so arrange its timing carefully.

If applying through an autoescuela, the school submits the examination application. The DGT examination application fee does not include the school's training charges. Ask the school to distinguish lessons, its administration charges, test-vehicle use and official fees.

sections.title: Understand retakes and provisional driving
paragraphs: DGT states that two unsuccessful attempts, whether in the same examination or across different tests, require a new application and fee. A passed test is retained for two years; if the licence is not obtained in that period, the tests must be taken again.

DGT provides free sample theory tests, but warns that the limited questionnaires are intended to familiarise you with the format rather than provide complete preparation. After passing the final examination, a provisional permit allows driving in Spain while awaiting the card. Do not treat it as an unrestricted international driving document.

sources.label: DGT: examination attempts, validity and provisional permit
